todo1.title: TODO 1: showBanner
whereToLook: Day 1 notes, M1 (Header, body, and call): showBriefing is a void method with no parameters, the same shape as showBanner.
A call statement is the method's name, empty parentheses, and a semicolon. It never repeats void or the modifiers.
The call goes at TODO 1 (call), above the length prompt, so the banner prints first.

todo2.title: TODO 2: showSweep
whereToLook: Day 1 notes, M2: a call is a statement, so a loop can repeat it.
Day 1 notes, P1 (Three kinds of argument): pass the loop variable sweep as the argument, the same way displayBurn(seconds) passes a variable.
The parameter needs a data type in the header: int, then a name.

todo3.title: TODO 3: displayData
whereToLook: Day 1 notes, P2 (Two parameters): every parameter needs its own data type, like (int high, int low).
Arguments match parameters by position, not by name. Pass length first, then width.
Calculate the area inside displayData and store it in a local variable named area before printing it.

todo4.title: TODO 4: showBeacons
whereToLook: Day 1 notes, P3 (Widening and a cast): a double argument can't go into an int parameter without a cast.
Keep the parameter an int. Put the cast in the call, the same way showThrust((int) precise) does.
A cast drops the decimal part: (int) 1.6 is 1. Don't round.
